learningObjective: Trace how uncleared parameter gradients and an unrestored evaluation mode persist into the next training batch as two independent state leaks.
mediumRationale: A compact two-lane Mermaid flowchart is the smallest useful representation of state surviving across batch boundaries; the spatial continuity makes the consequences of the two omitted reset operations explicit.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Selected: the learning task is to follow two state transitions across time, and a compact labelled flowchart expresses that ordering without custom geometry.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: deterministic SVG would duplicate Mermaid's node-and-arrow strengths while requiring hand-positioned text and more maintenance.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: ordered lists or a comparison table can name the states but do not show the omitted transitions carrying stale state into the next batch as directly.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: stepping through batches adds controls but no mechanism beyond the two fixed state traces.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: no reviewed source contains this exact paired gradient-buffer and module-mode trace with verified figure reuse permission.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose lists the bugs independently, but the hardest mental model is that both failures are persistent state crossing an iteration boundary.

pages.insight: The SAM slide includes optimizer.zero_grad between its first and second gradient computations, showing a specialized two-pass use rather than the ordinary per-batch lifecycle.
The preceding NLP slide defines preprocessing and word2vec components but does not show a complete training-state lifecycle.

The simple character-level language-model slide gives the directly relevant healthy order: model.train once, then device transfer, optimizer.zero_grad, forward, loss, backward, and optimizer.step for every batch.
The following tokenization-and-perplexity slide uses torch.no_grad for evaluation, but does not discuss model.eval or restoration of training mode.

deckReview.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI agent-6 (GPT-5.6 Sol) text-indexed all 214 pages for training-loop, optimizer, zero_grad, model.train, model.eval, no_grad, backpropagation, and gradient-accumulation references. The optimizer neighborhood on pages 46-51 and the complete directly relevant NLP neighborhood on pages 96-98 were read; pages 47 and 96-98 were also rendered and visually inspected. Page 97 is the closest source, while its neighbors establish that the deck treats no_grad separately and provides no paired persistent-state explanation. Later gradient-accumulation matches describe intentional effective-batch scaling, not this accidental stale-gradient bug. No deck wording, layout, code, or figure is reused.

sourceReview.notes: The shipped Mermaid composition is an original diagram derived from documented API semantics, not a redraw of a source figure. Its gradient lane distinguishes backward accumulation from optimizer.step: after batch one leaves g1 in .grad, batch two backward adds g2 unless zero_grad clears or removes the buffer. Its module lane separately shows eval mode persisting until train is called. The caption explicitly prevents a common conflation: no_grad controls autograd recording locally but does not restore module training mode.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, searched all 214 deck pages and inspected the relevant slide neighborhoods, checked official PyTorch API behavior and licensing, and selected an original compact state-flow diagram for the article's hardest cross-iteration mental model.

implementation.accessibility: The Mermaid block supplies an accessible title and a detailed description of both lanes. Every state and omitted reset is written directly in the nodes or on dashed missing-transition edges, so the lesson does not depend on color. The viz-compact marker opts out of the wide mobile minimum, allowing the top-to-bottom diagram to fit a 390 CSS-pixel viewport; established Mermaid theme variables provide dark-mode contrast, and shared print rules force a light high-contrast canvas with page-break avoidance.
